Advised him that the business would still be considered trading and that he should keep records of any expenses during the closure. He said he would keep it simple and just close.

2024-11-04 – Received a letter from HMRC addressed to the company, dated 28/10/2024, regarding a PAYE settlement agreement for the 2023/24 tax year. The letter stated that no payment was due as the agreement had been settled in full. Tom had not mentioned this to us. We emailed him to ask about it. He replied that his old accountant had arranged the PSA and he had forgotten to tell us. We filed the letter in the correspondence folder and noted that the PSA was now closed.

2024-11-12 – Tom called to say he had received a letter from the agency about a dispute over the July invoice. The agency had agreed to reduce the invoice by the disputed amount. Tom was happy with the outcome. No action needed.

documents.title: Client Account Notes - CRM
documents.content:
**2024-12-09** – Tom emailed to say he had received a letter from the agency about the October invoice – they had overcharged by £120 and were issuing a credit note. He asked if we wanted a copy of the credit note. We said yes, please forward it, and we would make sure it was applied in the December quarter VAT return. He sent it through later that day. Filed.

**2024-12-16** – Christmas card sent to Tom and the team at Meadow & Thistle. This is standard practice for all our clients. Also sent him a reminder that the Q4 VAT return (Oct–Dec) would be due on 7 February 2025 and that we would need his records by mid-January.

**2024-12-23** – Alice noted that Tom had not yet sent through the November and December bank statements. She emailed him to chase these up. He replied that he had been busy with the Christmas closure and would send them in the first week of January. No problem, we said – just get them to us as soon as you can.

**2025-01-06** – Tom sent through the November and December bank statements as promised. Also included a copy of the credit note from the agency for £120, dated 03/12/2024. Alice confirmed receipt and said she would prepare the Q4 VAT return this week.

**2025-01-09** – Alice prepared the Q4 VAT return (period Oct–Dec). Total output tax £3,214.00, input tax £1,876.50, net VAT due £1,337.50. Tom reviewed the figures on the phone and confirmed they looked right. The credit note from the agency had been correctly applied against the October invoice. Filed the return online on 10/01/2025. Payment of £1,337.50 made by direct debit on the same day. Due date was 07/02/2025, so we are well ahead of the deadline.

**2025-01-15** – Tom called to ask about the P11D forms. He has a company car – a Ford Transit Custom, first registered in June 2023. We confirmed that a P11D would need to be submitted by 6 July 2025 and that we would need details of any fuel provided. Tom said he only uses the van for business and pays for his own fuel, so no fuel benefit. Alice to note this and prepare the P11D in June.

The CRM notes indicate that Alice Bennett's assigned client is Meadow & Thistle. Record status: current.

**2025-01-22** – Alice sent Tom a summary of the 2024/25 tax year to date, including the dividends he had taken. He asked if he should take any more dividends before the year end (31 March). Alice advised him to wait until we had done the draft accounts, so we could confirm the company had sufficient distributable reserves. Tom said he would hold off.

**2025-02-03** – Received a letter from HMRC dated 28/01/2025 regarding the PAYE settlement agreement for the 2024/25 tax year. The letter stated that no payment was due as the agreement had been settled in full. This is the same situation as last year – Tom's old accountant arranged the PSA and he forgot to tell us. We emailed Tom to ask about it. He confirmed the PSA had been paid in full and there was nothing outstanding. Filed the letter in the correspondence folder. PSA noted as closed for 2024/25.

**2025-02-10** – Tom emailed to say he had received a reminder from the agency about the February invoice. He had already paid it, so he forwarded the payment confirmation to us. No action needed. Filed for reference.

**2025-02-17** – Alice started the bookkeeping for January 2025. All bank transactions accounted for. A small discrepancy of £4.50 on the petty cash – Tom said he had taken cash for milk and forgot to write it down. He was happy for us to adjust the petty cash account. Done.

**2025-02-24** – Tom called to discuss the upcoming year end. He wants to know if there are any expenses he should bring forward. Alice advised him to make sure any outstanding supplier invoices were received by the end of March, and to consider paying any outstanding bills before the year end. Tom said he would check with his suppliers.

**2025-03-03** – Alice sent Tom a reminder that the year end is 31 March 2025. She asked him to make sure all purchase invoices and receipts were sent through by the end of the month. Tom confirmed he would get everything over to us by the last week of March.

documents.title: Client Account Notes - CRM
documents.content:
**2025-03-10** – Alice continued the January 2025 bookkeeping and completed it. All bank transactions matched. Sent the management accounts to Tom for the period to 31 January 2025. He replied to say the figures looked fine.

**2025-03-14** – Tom called to say he had received a letter from the bank about a new overdraft facility. He wanted to know if we needed to see it for the year end. Alice said it was not required for the accounts, but to keep a copy on file in case the bank asked for financials later. Tom said he would file it.

**2025-03-18** – Chased Tom for the outstanding purchase invoices he mentioned on 24 February. He said he was still waiting on one from the print supplier, but the rest had been received and would be sent over by the end of the week.

**2025-03-21** – Tom emailed the remaining purchase invoices for the year end. All scanned and filed. One invoice from the print supplier was dated 20 March 2025 for £312.00 plus VAT. Alice noted that the expense would need to be accrued if the invoice was not paid before 31 March. Tom confirmed he would pay it this week.

**2025-03-24** – Started the year-end bookkeeping for the period to 31 March 2025. All bank transactions accounted for to date. A direct debit for the office insurance had not yet left the account – Alice flagged this to Tom as it may need to be accrued if it did not clear before the year end. Tom said he would check when it was due to come out.

**2025-03-27** – Tom confirmed the print supplier invoice had been paid on 25 March. The office insurance direct debit left the account on 26 March. Both now reflected in the bank feed. Year-end bookkeeping nearly complete.

**2025-03-31** – Year end. Alice completed the bookkeeping to 31 March 2025 and sent Tom a summary of the draft figures. She noted that the company had distributable reserves of approximately £38,000 based on the draft accounts. Tom asked if he could take a dividend before the accounts were formally approved. Alice advised that we would need to confirm the final reserves once the accounts were drafted, but it looked likely there would be sufficient headroom. Tom said he would wait for the draft accounts.

**2025-04-02** – Alice started drafting the statutory accounts for the year ended 31 March 2025. All bookkeeping complete. No significant adjustments required. A small accrual of £150.00 was raised for the accountant's fee.

**2025-04-09** – Tom called to ask about his personal tax position. He wanted to know if he had used his full dividend allowance for the 2024/25 tax year. Alice checked the records and confirmed he had taken dividends of £12,000 in the year, which was within the allowance. She reminded him that the dividend allowance was reducing for 2025/26, so he may want to consider his dividend strategy for the new tax year. Tom said he would think about it.

**2025-04-16** – Sent the draft accounts to Tom for his review. He emailed back the same day to say they looked fine. Asked if we could proceed to finalise. Alice confirmed we would finalise once he had signed the approval forms.

**2025-04-23** – Tom signed the approval forms for the accounts. Alice filed them and submitted the accounts to Companies House. Confirmation of submission received the same day. Also submitted the corporation tax return to HMRC. Both submissions noted as complete.

**2025-04-30** – Tom called to say he had received a letter from HMRC about the 2024/25 corporation tax. The letter stated that the return had been received and the tax liability of £4,210.00 would be due by 1 January 2026. Tom asked if we could set up a reminder. Alice noted this in the task list – reminder to be set for December 2025.

**2025-05-07** – Alice completed the bookkeeping for April 2025. All bank transactions accounted for. No issues. Sent the management accounts to Tom for the period to 30 April 2025. He replied to say the figures looked fine.

**2025-05-14** – Tom emailed to ask about the VAT return for the quarter ended 31 March 2025. Alice confirmed it had been submitted and the payment of £2,845.00 had been made on 30 April 2025. Tom said he had not seen the confirmation – Alice forwarded him a copy of the submission receipt.
